messages:
Zoe (Customer): hitting intermittent disconnects from our frontend when streaming with EventSource in Safari. sometimes we get half a response then it just stops. happens ~every 10-30s. no obvious 401/500 in our app logs. :confused:
Maya (Support): sorry to hear that — can you paste the exact request headers your browser is sending for the EventSource? Safari version? any CDN in front?
Zoe (Customer): Safari 16.6 and 17.2. We have Cloud CDN in front (fastly-ish). Request headers (copied from devtools):

User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10_15_7)...
Accept: text/event-stream
Origin: https://app.acme.example
Authorization: Bearer <redacted-token>

Maya (Support): thanks. two quick suspects: 1) CDN caching / 304s interfering with streamed responses, 2) Safari/EventSource and chunk boundaries + no keepalive comments. Can you check response headers from our API when the stream starts?
Zoe (Customer): response headers when a stream winds up (we captured a failing request):

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/event-stream
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600
ETag: "abc123"
Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://app.acme.example
Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true

Tom (Eng): ohhh public, max-age=3600 + ETag is a red flag for SSE. If the CDN or browser returns a 304 later or tries to cache that connection it can confuse streaming. Also Safari has known issues where it buffers until a CRLF chunk boundary or it expects keepalive comments.
Oliver (SRE): +1. Also check Vary: Authorization. If the CDN caches responses that vary by auth token and then returns 304, EventSource in Safari may not request the body and the client may see a silent stall.
Maya (Support): can you reproduce with curl so we can rule out client-side polyfill? run: curl -i -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream
Zoe (Customer): did that. here's the server trace around failure. server printed the lines below when it closed: 

[2026-02-03T14:02:11Z] connection open, stream id=xyz
data: {"chunk":"hello"}

[2026-02-03T14:02:21Z] sent keepalive comment
[2026-02-03T14:02:31Z] client closed unexpectedly (EPIPE)

No 401s. Cloud CDN logs show a 304 at 14:02:31 for the same url.
Tom (Eng): that matches: client closed at same time CDN returned 304 on a conditional request. Looks like some part of the stack issues a conditional GET mid-stream (maybe due to our upstream keepalive or a monitoring probe) and CDN responds 304 which Safari's EventSource doesn't handle gracefully.
Maya (Support): workaround while we triage: ensure server responds with Cache-Control: no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate for SSE endpoints and set Vary: Authorization. Also send frequent keepalive comments (every 10s) and ensure chunk size >= 2KB to avoid intermediate buffering in some Safari builds.
Tom (Eng): sample Express SSE handler to set safe headers: 

```js
app.get('/v1/stream', (req, res) => {
  res.set({
    'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream',
    'Cache-Control': 'no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate, max-age=0',
    'Pragma': 'no-cache',
    'Vary': 'Authorization',
    'Access-Control-Allow-Origin': req.headers.origin || '*',
    'Access-Control-Allow-Credentials': 'true',
    'Access-Control-Allow-Headers': 'Authorization,Content-Type',
  });
  res.flushHeaders();
  res.write(': keepalive\n\n'); // initial comment
  const t = setInterval(() => res.write(': heartbeat\n\n'), 10000);
  req.on('close', () => { clearInterval(t); });
});
```

Oliver (SRE): also ensure the CDN is configured not to cache that path (fastly: set a Cache-Control passthrough or a Cache-Bypass rule for /v1/stream). And definitely add Vary: Authorization so edge caches key by token.
Zoe (Customer): ok we deployed header changes and turned off caching in the edge for /v1/stream. still seeing occasional stalls in Safari 16.6 but much less frequent. any other possibilities?
Tom (Eng): there are three other items to check: 1) TLS session renegotiation or HTTP/1.1 proxy timeouts causing connectors to close, 2) Safari has a bug where very small chunks (<128 bytes) are buffered until connection end — try aggregating to slightly larger writes, 3) Auth refresh logic in your client: if the page attempts to re-open EventSource with a new Authorization header concurrently you can cause transient conditional GETs.
Maya (Support): can you also try the EventSource polyfill (github.com/Yaffle/EventSource or the whatwg-fetch streaming approach) as a diagnostic — if polyfill avoids stalls it's a Safari bug/trick. But polyfills may be heavier and should be treated as temporary.
Zoe (Customer): tried polyfill — it eliminated the stalls in 17.2 but still had a rare one in 16.6. polyfill is workable for now. Are there any server-side logs we should look for to flag this automatically?
Oliver (SRE): log these signals: conditional GETs (If-None-Match / If-Modified-Since) hitting /v1/stream, edge 304 responses, short chunk sizes (<256b), and connection resets (RST/EPIPE) within X seconds of last write. We can add an alert rule: if stream connections drop >1% in 5m with matching 304 in edge logs, page support alert.
Maya (Support): I'll update the support runbook with triage steps: reproduce with curl, check response headers, confirm CDN no-cache and Vary: Authorization, enable keepalive comments every 10s, try polyfill, bump chunk sizes, and gather edge logs for 304s. Adding note about billing spike risk: if client retries aggressively on reconnect it can cause token-based billing spikes; recommend exponential backoff in client reconnect logic. :warning:
Tom (Eng): one more note: for long-term we should add an endpoint-level lint in our deploy checks that forbids public caching headers on event-stream endpoints. Filing a small infra PR to auto-fail if Content-Type: text/event-stream AND Cache-Control contains public or max-age > 0.
Maya (Support): thanks team — Zoe, keep us posted. If you can capture a HAR of a failing session and attach the edge request/response ids we can correlate.
Zoe (Customer): will do; attaching two edge request ids when I have them. thanks all :pray:
support-bot: Incident guard: stream-stalls rule created for /v1/stream, threshold=1% over 5m.
eng-oncall: acknowledged and following up on infra lint task.
